roadmap.goal: Add the fitness-config-init skill that proposes a purpose-tuned fitness-config.json and writes it safely via the resolver.

phases.name: Walking skeleton and deterministic proposal gate
phases.description: Turn WS-1 green end-to-end (stdin proposal -> strict check -> canonical bytes -> fingerprint -> exclusive create), then lock canonical-bytes parity, the anchor-guarded baseline, and the strict validator with its rejections. Covers DISTILL implementation-order items 1-6.

steps.scenario_name: Priya saves a reviewed database-service config into ledgerd, which had none
criteria: Dry run on a folder without a config prints STATUS: would-create and Proposal: <fp>, then canonical JSON from a line exactly '{', writing nothing
Saving with --expect <fp> prints STATUS: created and the file bytes equal the canonical bytes shown by the dry run
The saved config passes validate --path . and strict validate fitness-config.json; show --path . prints Config: fitness-config.json
The workspace state delta shows exactly one new file; with target equal to anchor no config above the anchor is read
WS-1 passes and the fitness-config-per-directory suite stays green

steps.description: Extend validate_config per ADR-008 (names, numeric 0-100, no bool, version 1, two-number ranges, all violations, no crash) and reject invalid proposals with named reasons; settle partial-weights semantics and update ADR-008.
steps.scenario_name: A proposal whose weights add up to 101 is never saved
criteria: Invalid proposals (sum 101, outline flaws, non-object stdin, unbalanced save) get STATUS: invalid, reasons name the domain or section, sum errors show 101 and 100
Validating a hand-edited config with a 'usability' weight and cutoff 'high' fails, names both problems, and prints no traceback
The example and a cutoff-only override still validate; the stdlib validator rejects every sample the JSON Schema rejects when jsonschema is installed
Partial override weights like {"weights": {"data": 30}} validate alone; sum-to-100 applies to the merged config; init-written configs are complete (10 domains, integers, sum 100)

phases.name: Write-gate guarantees, override chain and CI
phases.description: Harden the write gate (fingerprint mismatch, missing --expect, existing file, damaged chain, OS write failure, post-write verify and rollback), announce overrides in the chain, and wire pytest plus the resolver audit into CI. Covers DISTILL items 7-8 and DEVOPS note 9.1.

steps.name: Reviewed-proposal guarantees with verify and rollback
steps.description: Refuse any save that is not the reviewed proposal, refuse existing files without --force, stop on a damaged ancestor, leave no partial or temp file on OS write failure, and verify-then-roll-back after writing.
steps.scenario_name: A proposal that differs from the one Priya reviewed is never saved
criteria: A fingerprint differing from --expect reports fingerprint-mismatch; --from without --expect or --dry-run exits non-zero with stderr mentioning --expect; nothing is written
An existing config without --force reports refused-exists with its bytes and mtime unchanged
A malformed ancestor config stops the check and names the damaged file
A read-only target folder exits non-zero with no success token, no traceback, and no leftover config or temp file
test_write_gate.py proves via an injected writer that verification failure restores prior bytes and reports verify-failed-rolled-back, and that a concurrent create is refused
steps.implementation_notes:
DISTILL order item 7. Activates milestone-2 'A proposal that differs from the one Priya reviewed is never saved', 'A proposal cannot be saved without the fingerprint from a check', 'An existing config is never replaced without Priya's go-ahead', 'A damaged config higher up stops the check and names the damaged file', 'A folder Priya cannot write to is left without a partial config'. Write-gate sequence per data-models.md 6.2 and ADR-010: recompute fingerprint, pre-check ancestors, temp file in the same dir then os.replace (exclusive create without --force), re-read, compare fingerprint, validate_effective, roll back on mismatch. The writer is the single impure adapter, passed in as a function so tests substitute it (Earned Trust: fault injection of silent no-op, partial write, concurrent create). Acceptance-review issue 3 and 4 behaviours are fixed here.
